newsitem.title: USA: US appeals panel denies review of Cochran ruling.
newsitem.headline: US appeals panel denies review of Cochran ruling.

text.p: A federal appeals court in Denver has rejected a U.S. Justice Dept. request that it reconsider its decision overturning the fraud convictions of ex-Stifel, Nicolaus & Co executive Robert Cochran.

"We are pleased that the court has accepted our position and that it will not hear further argument on this case," Cochran defense attorney B.J. Rothbaum said Thursday when contacted about the June 4 ruling by the entire 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.
A three-member panel of the 10th circuit in late March had unanimously reversed a federal jury's conviction of Cochran on eight charges of wire fraud and money laundering.

The charges involved side fees that Cochran allegedly received in helping issuers find a good rate on investment contracts for millions of dollars of bonds issued by the Oklahoma City Airport Trust and Sisters of St. Mary Healthcare System.

In early May, Justice asked the full appeals court to rehear that part of the case dealing with the airport trust bonds, which were issued as taxable securities. The healthcare bonds had been issued as tax-exempts.
But the panel on Wednesday refused to grant the so-called "en banc" review of the decision.
A Justice spokesman was unavailable for comment.
A Securities and Exchange Commission spokesman also was unavailable for comment. The SEC also had urged the 10th Circuit to reconsider the ruling in a friend of the court brief last month.
